chapter: Army cornet and Bix's Bach horn
title: A new Benge horn after the war
summary: After the war Benge replaces his battered horn with a new one; Johnston praises hearing it.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Oh, but anyway that was the great Benge horn and then after you came back from the War he made another one for you right?

Yes. Eldon Benge, I came back and my poor Benge horn was all battered up you know from going and travelling all over there over the years, two and a half years in Europe. So I'm playing now the 'Brass Rail' again and Alvin came in one night. He had been in previously and so you know we were talking about the horn and I told him what happened. And he came in and he said, Jimmy, he said, give me your old horn. And I gave it to him and he handed me a brand new one, a brand new Benge horn. Wasn't that sweet of him?
Now is that the one that you're blowing, that's the one you're blowing now?
That's the one I blew just now. Tried to blow. (LAUGHTER). My chops are not warmed up.

No I think even posterity will realise that I called upon you rather suddenly to blow this and that you didn't have a chance to really warm up. But I think, well I just want to say this, that I think anybody listening to your records of course will have no doubt about the kind of musician you are. But I do think that it's historically important for us to hear this horn and to hear you blow the thing that created such a sensation during the War in Scotland. And I don't think there is any need to apologise really. Of course I read it in Time Magazine myself. Yes I know, that's one of the reasons I wanted you to do it so badly.
